_about: Per-tab CCL manifests (voice_guide_redesign.md sections 3, 8, 9). Each tab declares its supported verbs (caps) and its knob dimensions with a DOM binding + spoken aliases. Consumed by BOTH the shell (explorer.html builds the active tab's ctx from this) and the coverage audit (every live interactive control on a tab must be a bound knob or an explicit exclusion -- unbound control => loud pre-push failure, section 9). Adding a T1 tab is ONE entry here plus a knowledge default file -- never a new tool, prompt, or session-schema change. Knob `values[].v` are the real DOM option values (NOT their display labels); `aka` are the spoken forms a user would say. A knob carries `aka` too, because the word PRINTED on a control is not always its id -- metabolism's `metric` select is labelled Amplitude on screen, so `label` must mirror the live UI text and `aka` must cover what a user would actually say. Knob names and aliases MUST be single tokens: the parser takes `set <knob> <value...>` and reads the knob as the first word, so a two-word alias is unparseable, not merely unmatched. Keys beginning with _ are documentation and ignored by consumers. GESTURES: each tab must also declare its non-DOM interaction surface (zoom, pan, drag, click, hover) -- the runtime sweep enumerates ELEMENTS and is structurally blind to gestures, so they are declared and the gate checks the declaration is honest: `covered` must name verbs the tab actually has in caps, `deferred` must name its increment, `excluded` must give a reason, and a tab declaring nothing FAILS (silence is not a completeness claim).

sociogram._knobs_note: Sociogram's affordances are filters/selection/highlight/camera (their own dim kinds, not `set` knobs). It carries no `set` verb in v1. Listed here so the shell can read one uniform per-tab source; its caps mirror the engine's SOCIOGRAM_CAPS until step 2 migrates the shell to read caps from this file.

community_explorer._caps_note:
Increment 1 reached and walked the cards. Increment 2 adds the GRAPH sub-view's own dimensions: the eight type filters (show/hide/only/all/none and the journal verbs that ride on them), the Q3 gate as a knob, Fit All, and a roster of the graph's nodes with open/close. Still absent and still deferred below with their real blockers: find (the tab's search HIGHLIGHTS rather than filters, so the Sociogram's opacity-derived read would call a dimmed node gone), and zoom/pan (d3's behaviour is a lexical const here, so the only road is synthetic wheel/mouse events on #graph).
Caps are per TAB and the rosters here are per SUB-VIEW, so `open` and `fit` are advertised on the cards view too and refuse there by name. That refusal is the honest one, not a leak of the Sociogram's function names -- see the `when` gates on `filters` and `camera`.

knobs.label: Exemplary (Q3) only
knobs._note: The one deferred control that needed nothing built: a real <input type=checkbox> in the tab's own document, the same shape metabolism's `logy` already uses. It composes with the type filters by AND (nodeVisible tests both), so `set exemplary on` narrows whatever cut is already up rather than replacing it.

community_explorer._views_note: Two sub-views with two different rosters. `go cards` rides on the existing `go` rather than adding a verb, the same call made for tab order. The cards view lazy-loads a nested app, so entry announces the roster when it arrives rather than claiming zero.

items._note: The grid renders CARD_LIMIT (60) of the matching set; the page's own status line carries the true total, so `what` says '60 of 1006' rather than '60'.

THE SVG CASE: elements in the DOM with data bound to them. `#graph circle` selects exactly the nodes and nothing else -- gLinks appends `line`, gLabels appends `text`, gNodes is the only thing appending `circle`, and there is no <circle> in the markup or the CSS -- so the roster is non-positional without the page gaining a class it does not have. A <circle> carries no text, hence `label.datum`: d3 parks the node object on the element, so the name is a DOM read.
`activate: "click"` reaches the page's own `.on('click', (ev,n) => showNode(n))` with the right node object, which is why showNode taking an object rather than an id costs nothing. `selected` is scoped to `#rightpanel.open` because the panel keeps its last contents after it is closed -- the `.open` class is the page's own marker for what is actually up, and reading the h3 without it would report a stale heading as the current selection.
NO `total`, deliberately, and this is the opposite call from the cards spec above. #stats reads 'N communities - M edges' where N is the VISIBLE count: rebuild() does .exit().remove(), so DOM presence IS the filter truth and drawn == matching. Declaring it as `total` would produce 'N of N' forever, which is a number that cannot disagree with itself and therefore says nothing.
DO NOT infer visibility from opacity here. applyLens dims non-matching nodes to 0.08 instead of removing them, because search on this tab HIGHLIGHTS and never filters (2026-05-29 lock); getClientRects is the right test and an opacity-derived one would read a dimmed node as gone.

filters._note:
ONE AXIS, EIGHT LEAVES, AND NOT ONE LINE OF STATE READ FROM THE PAGE. The roster comes from `keys` -- the checkboxes' own data-type attributes -- because this page keeps its truth in `const activeTypes = new Set(...)`: a lexical binding, so window.activeTypes is undefined, and a Set, so the key->boolean shape the shell used to assume means nothing here. The controls carry the same information and need no page access, which is the tell that reading the CONTROLS was always the general case and reading a window map was prs_3d's special one.
`leaf` is `{clean}` rather than the default slug: these keys are display names ('Civic & Political'), and `civic-&-political` is a group name, not something to say or hear. `{slug}` still exists and still means 'reproduce the page's own id convention' -- prs_3d needs exactly that and must not get this.
`all` is `{on, off}` because all and none are two `<span class="allnone">` here, not one master checkbox: spans, so not even buttons, and the road is `.click()`. Note that a span is INVISIBLE to the audit sweep (CONTROL_SEL matches inputs, buttons and roles) -- these two are named here because nothing in the gate would otherwise know they exist.
`when` scopes the whole dimension to the graph sub-view: on the cards view the left panel is display:none and the cards app filters by its own controls, so an ungated spec would advertise eight checkboxes nobody is looking at.
filters._read_note: Reads come back off `.checked`, not off a state object -- the RENDERED truth, which is the contract every other read on this surface follows and the only one of the two that exists on this page at all.

camera._note:
ONE VERB, AND IT IS A BUTTON. Fit All is an anonymous listener on #btn-fit -- there is no exported name to call, and under the no-page-edits rule there is no way to give it one, so the camera spec names the click. That is the mouse's road, which this thread prefers to a function call anyway.
NO zoom / pan / rotate / spin. The page's d3 zoom behaviour and its svg selection are top-level `const`s, invisible to a window path, so the remaining road is synthetic wheel/mouse events dispatched at #graph (d3 v7 binds wheel.zoom and mousedown.zoom on the selection, and parks the current transform on the element as `__zoom`). Reasoned from d3's behaviour, not run -- deferred below until one dispatched wheel event proves it.
`when` gates the whole spec: #btn-fit lives in a header group the tab hides on the cards sub-view, and a hidden button still answers .click(), so an ungated camera would report 'fit' for a graph nobody is looking at.

dim_coverage.note: the eight type filters, reached by show/hide/only/all/none through the declared `filters` section. The all/none spans are not swept (they are spans) and are named in the filters note instead.

close -- the right panel. Named by the graph items spec, so the audit counts it there. (A span, so not actually swept; listed for the reader.)

curriculum_tools._caps_note: The first tab whose roster lives BEHIND the click. Parts and questions start closed, so `pick`/`next` -- which only ever MARKED an item -- could reach nothing here at all: with the tree collapsed there is nothing revealed to pick from, and no verb that opens it. So this tab is the one that made `open` general. `open` existed already but was wired to openNodeByLabel, a global that lives on wiki_narration.html and nowhere else, which is why every tab since the Sociogram has had to leave it out of caps. It is now DECLARED per item spec (`activate`), the same way `frame` and `total` are.

knobs.label: Show article rows
knobs._note: Not a display preference. With it OFF, clicking a QUESTION stops expanding and jumps straight to that question's first available article (onClickQuestion) -- so the identical spoken command would mean two different things depending on a checkbox the voice user cannot see. The items spec therefore declares `requires_knob` and the shell puts it ON before walking, out loud (Tom, 2026-07-27: bind it, force it on before pick).

knobs.label: Summa-in-1-year Transcript
knobs._note: A SETTING, not a place: it changes how the open article is rendered, not which article you are on -- so it is a knob rather than a sub-view. It is drawn as two buttons, which knobs could not bind (a <select> or a checkbox only), and its winning class is `.on`, not the `.active` a view's test hard-codes. Declaring it as a view would have been mis-declaring it to fit the machinery; the `buttons` bind kind is the honest fix and is portable to every button-group toggle in the fan-out. Both sides are gated on the entry actually HAVING that file (switchMode returns early otherwise), and neither does anything until an article is open.

curriculum_tools._views_note: `sociogram` names a real TAB as well, the third such collision in six manifests, and it is a TRUE sub-view rather than a name to rename away: it pulls in the Sociogram tool pre-cut to Summa nodes via applySummaSociogramPreset (Tom, 2026-07-27: 'just as under the Agent Map'). No new mechanism was needed -- 69c312d already settled this exact case: standing on a tab, that tab's own view wins, `go sociogram tab` forces the tool, and `go sociogram of curriculum tools` works from anywhere. Entering it LAZILY fetches wiki_narration.html, a ~28.7 MB artifact, on first entry: going there is a real download, not a toggle -- the same warning the Agent Map's sociogram view carries.

requires_knob.why: with it off, a question click jumps to an article instead of expanding, so `open` would have two meanings

items._note:
ONE FLAT ROSTER OF VISIBLE ROWS at all three levels, not three level-scoped rosters. `when` can only ask which sub-view is active, and nothing on this page says which LEVEL a user is walking -- there is no such state to read, because a sighted user is not at a level either, they are looking at an open tree. So `next` walks exactly the visual reading order and `open` on a part or a question expands it, which makes the roster GROW as you go. That growth is reported, because expanding a container and loading an article are the same verb on the same tree and would otherwise sound identical.
NO `total` DECLARED, deliberately. #stats-line counts ARTICLES (2656 of 2747 available) while this roster counts ROWS; wiring it up would make `what` say '24 of 2747 entries', which is false in unit rather than merely imprecise. Speaking the availability line honestly is its own declaration -- curriculum tools increment 2.
`.a-row.avail` only: 91 articles have no transcript yet and carry NO click handler at all, so offering them would be offering a door that does not open.
items._reads_note: Where the page PUTS what a row opens -- the RENDERED MARKDOWN, not the pane around it. #content-area was the first guess and it wrapped the article in the page's own chrome: the reader opened with the ref, the title, the day, and then read the two mode buttons aloud ('Summa-in-1-year Transcript', 'Contemporary Synthesis?') before reaching a word of Aquinas. It also hid every per-block filter, because the whole article arrived as ONE child node whose textContent carried the provenance blockquotes and headings inside it. #md-body is the markdown itself, so its children are the blocks and the reader can tell prose from furniture. Without it `read` spoke the tree row -- 'A1 Article 1 Day 2', five words -- and called it the article.
items._read_variants_note: One article, two renderings. Asked for 'the commentary', a human guide turns to it and reads -- they do not explain that a toggle exists, and then wait to be asked again (Tom, 2026-07-27). A variant is NOT a new dimension: it writes the `mode` knob the tab already has, so `set mode synthesis` and `read the commentary` end in the same state. The read waits for the page's fetch, because reading straight after the click would speak the PREVIOUS rendering and announce it as the new one.
items._locate_note: An ADDRESS, which is none of the things `go` already resolves -- not a tab, not a sub-view, not a link. Summa's refs are I.Q4.A2 and only Summa knows that, so the scheme is declared and the shell only knows how to read `locate`. A level left unsaid is taken from where the user already is (the part of the question currently open) and the guess is SAID, because a wrong part is a plausible-sounding wrong answer rather than an obvious failure. `open_first` opens closed ancestors, since a target inside a collapsed container is addressable but not reachable -- marking it silently would be pointing at a shut door.
items._search_note: What a docent knows without knowing everything: not the Summa by heart, but roughly where things live, and how to look (Tom, 2026-07-27: 'take me to a question on angelic knowledge'). The tab already holds all 611 question titles in its own indexData at boot, so this is a plain title match -- deliberately NOT a model call or an embedding. Deterministic, free, testable, and it never bills the broker. QUESTIONS ONLY in this increment: article titles are mostly null in the index (the row renders 'Article N'), so searching them would return a list of indistinguishable numbers. Resolved LAST in the `go` chain, after tabs, views, coordinates, renderings and links, because it is the broadest net and must never shadow something named outright. One clear winner lands; anything else is named back, since silently choosing among four is indistinguishable from being right when there is no screen.

items._note: The Summa sociogram is the wiki_narration graph one document down, pre-cut to Summa nodes. Its nodes are walkable in principle -- revealedNodes() already knows this exact artifact -- but that reader is hard-wired to the tab's OWN document (ifWin/ifDoc) and does not take a frame the way domItems does. Generalising it is the prs_3d increment's job, not this one's, so the view is reachable and honest about being unwalkable rather than silently returning an empty roster.

prs_3d._caps_note: THE FIRST TAB WITH NO ELEMENTS TO WALK. Its 507 narratives are drawn into a WebGL canvas -- the whole tab is one <div id="canvas-container"> -- so there is nothing for domItems to enumerate and nothing for getClientRects to be asked about. The Sociogram looks like the same case and is not: d3 leaves an SVG circle per node behind, which is why revealedNodes could read `.node-circle` and pass for the general adapter. It never was one; it was the SVG case. So the roster here is read from the page's OWN data (`meshes`, the three.js scene objects) through declared dotted paths, and `open` is a declared CALL rather than a click -- see the items spec. The FILTER dimension is declared too (see `filters`), so this tab cuts data by voice on all three of its axes. NO `find` yet: the highlight dim reads a class stamp off SVG opacities and `search` ends in el.click(), both DOM-shaped. The CAMERA, by contrast, is now declared -- see `camera`. It was deferred for exactly one session on the grounds that execCamera was Sociogram-specific, and Tom's answer was the right one: a tab built around an orbiting camera that voice cannot turn is a room the guide can walk up to and never walk around.

knobs.label: Edges (threads)
knobs._note: The P-R-S threads within one narrative. A bool rather than a member of the Sociogram's `edges` FAMILY on purpose: that family is a `showEdgeType` map batch-written through refreshSimLinks, and this tab has three independent booleans and one applyPRSFilters. Inheriting the family binds would be the exact mistake the Community Explorer manifest was warned off (2026-07-26).

prs_3d._knobs_note: Three booleans, no `views`. NO SUB-VIEWS AT ALL here, which is worth saying out loud because the standing trap of this fan-out is a view whose name is also a tab: three of the first six collided (2026-07-26). This tab has one surface, so there is nothing to collide.

items._note:
ONE ITEM IS THREE MESHES. A PRS narrative is drawn as a problem, a resource and a solution sharing one triplet id, so without `dedupe` the guide would walk every narrative three times and report a count the page itself contradicts -- updatePrsCount dedupes by triplet id for exactly this reason, and `total` reads that same line so the two numbers cannot drift.
`visible` is the page's own three.js flag, which is what applyPRSFilters writes: it is the same question getClientRects answers in the DOM, asked where this page keeps the answer.
`activate` names prsSearchClickResult, which is what the page's OWN search results call -- so voice opens a narrative by the same road a click does, including the camera move onto it. That matters more here than anywhere: with 507 nodes in three dimensions, selecting something off-screen and saying nothing would be indistinguishable from doing nothing.
NO SORT, unlike the Sociogram's alphabetical roster. Source order is the order the page built them, grouped by tradition and then by date; the labels open "P1 (Text, referenced in ...)" so sorting them alphabetically would produce an order that means nothing to anyone.
items._selected_note: A window PATH, not a selector, because a canvas has nothing to carry a class. Same rule as Summa's `.a-row.sel` -- read the PAGE's marker rather than the click we just made -- and it is what closes the FIFTH which-document instance the 2026-07-27 handoff said to expect: `read` decides what to call the thing by asking whether the marked ELEMENT is still attached, which a canvas roster can never answer yes to, so the reader fell through to #right-page-title (absent here) and called a narrative "this article".
items._label_note: 222 OF THE 453 NARRATIVES HAVE NO LABEL AT ALL -- the field is present and empty in the source data, and the page's own info panel opens with a blank <h3> for them. Without the fallback the guide skipped every one: it said "231 narratives here" over a tab drawing 453, and half the artifact was unreachable by voice because of a gap in the data rather than anything about the tab. The fallback is the narrative's PROBLEM, clipped: it is always present, it is what the node actually is, and it is the one string a user could plausibly say back ("open positive geometry"). Clipping can make two narratives share a handle; matchItems then names both and asks, which is the right failure. Fixing the underlying data is a job for the generator, not for the guide -- but the guide must not pretend the unnamed ones are not there.

continuous field, the same exclusion the Sociogram's #date-slider carries. The DISCRETE year filter beside it (the per-decade checkboxes) is the reachable form of the same idea and is deferred, not excluded

a BOOL DRAWN AS ONE BUTTON that toggles its own .active class. The three bind kinds are checkbox, select and a button GROUP (v -> sel); a single button fits none of them, and declaring it as a group of two entries pointing at the same selector would be mis-declaring it to fit the machinery -- the thing the `buttons` bind was invented to avoid

Deferred is not a synonym for excluded -- everything under controls_deferred is IN scope and reachable by hand today, and the shell test asserts the count exactly so a new control cannot quietly join the list.

gestures.note: rotate left|right swings round the vertical axis, up|down raises and lowers the eye, in the page's own clamped range. `spin left|right` is the same turn left running -- the one command here that does not end when the sentence does, which is why it has its own off switch and why `stop` halts it too.

orbit._idle_note: This view drifts on its own at load until the first drag or wheel. Declaring the flag lets the shell see a turning view it did not start, so `spin off` and `stop` act on what the user is actually watching instead of on our own timer.

camera._note:
AN ORBIT CAMERA IS THREE NUMBERS AND A POINT. theta swings round the vertical axis, phi raises and lowers the eye, radius is the viewing distance, and cameraTarget is what it looks at; updateCameraPosition is the page's own function that turns the four into a camera position. Every camera verb is a step on one of them, so the declaration is paths and step sizes rather than code -- the same rule the item spec follows.
The numbers are the PAGE's, not invented: the clamps mirror onWheel (15..120) and the drag handler's phi guard (0.1 .. PI*0.85), so voice can never put the camera somewhere the mouse cannot. The orbit step is 0.4 rad, about what an 80-pixel drag does at the page's own 0.005 rad/px; the pan step is a quarter of the current viewing distance, so it feels the same close in and far out, exactly as the graph's pan scales with zoom.
PAN USES THE CAMERA'S OWN RIGHT AND UP, read off its world matrix. Panning along world axes would send the view sideways in a direction unrelated to what the user is looking at -- which after any rotation is nearly always.

filters._note:
THREE INDEPENDENT AXES, ONE FLAT ROSTER -- which is exactly what the engine already wanted. resolveGroups resolves `section/leaf` keys, so declaring the sections gives `only levin`, `hide disciplines`, `only cognitive`, `none` and the ambiguity hedge with no new grammar and no new verbs. The Sociogram namespaces its own keys the same way (traditions/levin, structure/architecture); the difference was never the shape of the roster, only that the shell read it from one page's `groupVisibility`.
WRITES GO THROUGH THE CHECKBOX, not the state object: the shell sets `checked` and dispatches `change`, so the page's own prsToggleThinker / prsToggleDisc / prsToggleYear run with their own apply chains. That matters here and is not ceremony -- disciplines must redraw the wedge meshes (applyDiscFilters) and years the decade rings (applyYearFilters) BEFORE the node pass, and the traditions handler keeps the All box in step. Writing prsFilterState directly would set the data cut and leave the drawing behind it, which is the class of bug this whole design keeps finding.
`leaf` exists because the spoken name is not always the state key. Decades are numbers in the page and "the 1990s" out loud, so years declare `{k}s`; disciplines are two words in the page and must be ONE token to a parser that splits on spaces, so they slug to `cognitive-science` -- and `only cognitive` still lands by prefix.
filters._all_note: `all` and `none` go through each section's own master checkbox rather than sweeping every key, so the page does its own sweep -- one dispatch per section instead of thirty-four, and no chance of the master box disagreeing with the boxes under it.
